answer: Slot-auction bonds resist sybils: a fixed number of new-identity seats open each epoch and are sold by a descending-price auction, so the bond is whatever the market clears — mass registration bids that price up until minting a swarm becomes ruinous. The clearing price is a live signal of registration demand, a prism splitting raw sign-up pressure into a cost each applicant must pay. An honest joiner buys one seat cheaply in a quiet epoch; a farm chasing a thousand seats watches its own bids mirror back as a soaring bond it cannot cover.
